item.title: 4 killed in U.S. strike on alleged drug-smuggling boat in Caribbean, Pentagon says
item.description: The latest attack brings the number of people who have been killed in boat strikes by the U.S. military in Latin America to at least 231 in 69 strikes since the Trump administration began targeting those it calls "narcoterrorists" about one year ago.

item.title: Sheeran says situation in Gaza is "catastrophic and unjustifiable" at Philly show
item.description: Ed Sheeran opened his solo concert in Philadelphia on Saturday with comments about Gaza, saying what is happening there is "catastrophic and unjustifiable."

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Sept. 20)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: U.S. touts number of barrels of oil escorted through Strait by U.S. military
item.description: The U.S. military has escorted one billion barrels of oil and over 2,000 commercial vessels out of the Persian Gulf in the last couple of months, the Pentagon said.

item.title: UMass Dartmouth football player killed in stabbing, student charged with murder
item.description: A UMass Dartmouth football player was killed in a stabbing in Providence and another student has been charged with murder.

item.title: Lawsuits filed over Nazi-looted art displayed in museums in Los Angeles, Auschwitz
item.description: Between 1933 and 1945, the Nazi regime orchestrated the largest art theft in world history, seizing over 600,000 works of art across Europe from Jewish families, collectors and museums.

item.title: From 2013: Cher on Bob Mackie, clothes and fashion statements
item.description: In this web exclusive recorded in 2013, Cher talked with correspondent Anthony Mason about her relationship with clothes, and her decades-long work with costume designer Bob Mackie, who dressed her for "The Sonny & Cher Show," TV specials, and stage productions. [Mackie died on Sept. 14, 2026 at age 87.]

item.title: Book excerpt: "Roll the Calls" by Ari Emanuel
item.description: In his memoir, the Hollywood superagent and mogul writes of coming to blows in the competitive entertainment universe – and, in one instance, being sidelined by the business end of a truck.

item.title: Trump vows to form "AI Force," says he won't allow slowdown of AI development
item.description: In a Truth Social post​, Mr. Trump called fears around artificial intelligence possibly becoming a superintelligence that could pose a threat to human existence a hoax.

item.title: CNN, MS NOW and Politico staffers barred from White House after Trump ban
item.description: President Trump said Friday that three outlets would be banned from the White House, "effective immediately."

item.title: Lawsuit says AI giants made illegal deal on technology's slowdown
item.description: The lawsuit argues the leading AI companies violated antitrust laws when they agreed to coordinate slowdown efforts.

item.title: Low and slow barbecue greets Tex-Mex tastes at Hurtado BBQ
item.description: Chef and pitmaster Brandon Hurtado blends Texas tastes with Mexican American barbecue traditions at Hurtado BBQ.

item.title: "What Not to Wear" stylist Stacy London shares new digital closet organizing service Starmoire
item.description: "What Not to Wear" stylist Stacy London and co-founder Ruth Foxe Blader share all about their new digital closet organizing service, Starmoire.

item.title: How superstar Juanes is helping build sustainable homes after Colombia's devastating earthquake
item.description: Latin superstar Juan Esteban, known as Juanes, has won 29 Grammys and sold out venues across the world. He joined Lilia Luciano to discuss his career, new work and giving back to his home country of Colombia in a time of great need.

item.title: How Apple's risky retail venture made profits boom
item.description: Ron Johnson, Apple's former senior vice president of retail, explains how the tech company welcomed physical shoppers in his book, "Shop Different: How Retail Revealed Apple's Genius."

item.title: Denmark and Greenland leaders cautiously optimistic after U.S. security deal
item.description: President Trump announced he struck a deal to give the U.S. "permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland, completely addressing ALL of our many U.S. concerns."

item.title: Exclusive discounts from CBS Mornings Deals
item.description: On this edition of CBS Deals, we show you items that will help improve your everyday lifestyle. Visit cbsdeals.com to take advantage of these exclusive deals today. CBS earns commissions on purchases made through cbsdeals.com.

item.title: Miss USA 2026 is the first married woman and mother to be crowned
item.description: Justus Kelley made history after she became the first married woman and the first mom to earn the Miss USA sash and crown. Kelley shares her experience with the iconic pageant and speaks about her philanthropic work.

item.title: Trump announces U.S. will control Greenland's security after deal with Denmark
item.description: President Trump says that the U.S. and Denmark have reached an agreement for the U.S. to have "permanent control" over Greenland's security.

item.title: Patrick Clancy says he still talks to his kids "all the time"
item.description: In an exclusive interview airing Sunday on 60 Minutes, Patrick Clancy shares his side of the story, just weeks after his ex-wife Lindsay Clancy's murder trial ended without a verdict. Ross Douthat sat down with Patrick Clancy to discuss life after trauma and what lies ahead.

item.title: Inside a U.S. aircraft carrier launching attacks on Iran
item.description: CBS News' Tom Hanson took an exclusive tour of the USS George Washington, one of two U.S. aircraft carriers in the region launching attacks against Iran.

item.title: How the NYPD is preparing for the U.N. General Assembly
item.description: The United Nations General Assembly kicks off next week. President Trump and foreign leaders, including Benjamin Netanyahu, are expected to speak. Anna Schecter spoke to the NYPD about security efforts.

item.title: Trump says he'll bar CNN, MS NOW, Politico reporters from White House "effective immediately"
item.description: President Trump says he will bar CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House. Trump added that other media outlets could be added to his ban.

item.title: 9/19: Saturday Morning
item.description: President Trump bans some journalists from the White House, how Apple broke into retail, plus Tex-Mex barbecue on The Dish.

item.title: Trump says he's banning CNN, Politico and MS NOW from the White House
item.description: CBS News observed two MS NOW employees being turned away from the White House on Saturday morning.

item.title: Cuba power grid collapse leaves millions without electricity again
item.description: One Cuba resident said there is "no way to know" when power will be restored to the island nation.

item.title: Firefighters struggle with staffing shortages amid record wildfire season
item.description: Wildfires have burned more than 8.5 million acres of land in the U.S. this year, and at the peak of the season, there weren't enough people or equipment to fight them.

item.title: Appeals court rejects Trump's third-country deportation policy
item.description: A federal appeals court ruled Friday that U.S. immigration officials must offer detainees "a meaningful opportunity to contest" any deportation to countries where they have no ties.

item.title: Patrick Clancy: "I think I did the best I could"
item.description: Asked whether he feels like he failed in some way, Patrick Clancy told 60 Minutes he believes he did the best he could with the information he had at the time.

item.title: RFK Jr. tells anti-vaccine activists they have a "friend in the White House"
item.description: Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. spoke at a conference hosted by an organization he once led that has promoted doubts about vaccines.
